newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning.
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Indian stocks likely to remain nervous this week as wary investors brace for political and economic setbacks, brokers say. The benchmark Bombay index closed last week 92.05 points or 2.7 percent lower at 3254.73
** Market awaits the possible arrest of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, who has been ordered to appear in court on Monday in a criminal conspiracy case
Rao's plea for protection against possible arrest was turned down last week
** State-run refining firm Bharat Petroleum Corp puts off public equity issue worth 4.12 billion rupees -- which was due to open in late October -- until market sentiment improves
** Voting begins in India's northern Uttar Pradesh in the first round of crucial three-phase local assembly elections

The polls will see Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's fractious United Front alliance take on the Congress party, which supports his minority government in New Delhi, and the BJP in a triangular fight for the state's 425-member Vidhan Sabha, or lower house
Uttar Pradesh sends 85 deputies to the 545-member federal parliament, where the BJP is the biggest single party.
** Indian banks stay closed on half-yearly closure of bank accounts
MARKETS:
** On Friday, Indian shares fell broadly in jittery trade triggered by political worries, traders say
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 52.32 points or 1.58 percent lower at 3254.73
** The 100-share National index fell 18.18 points or 1.23 percent to 1459.42
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** A decline in cash generation by companies last year accounts for this year's slow down in corporate growth. A study shows cash generated from operations by some top corporates fell by almost half in 1996 compared to the previous year, Economic Times newspaper reports
** Sales of medium-sized passenger cars, within the price range of 400,000 to 700,000 rupees, grew by just one percent during April-August 1996, weekend Financial Express reports
** Board of Padmini Polymers to meet to decide on bonus issue and raising international equity or debt
** Annual shareholders meeting of Indian Oil Corporation at 0530 GMT in Bombay
** Automobile firm PAL-Peugeot to lift month-long lockout at its unit in suburban Bombay from October 1, Economic Times reports
